description: How each ODS core service runs on native Windows, without Docker or WSL. The desktop app's Extensions page and docs/WINDOWS-NATIVE-MIGRATION-PLAN.md both read this list. status: built-in (ships today), next (the next milestone), planned, needs-design (needs a maintainer decision), external (use the vendor's Windows app), not-planned.

services.approach: Official ggml-org llama.cpp Windows builds (CUDA 13.1/12.4, Vulkan, CPU, ARM64), pinned by SHA-256, verified before every launch and supervised in a Windows job object.
This desktop app is the control center: setup, status, models, logs, diagnostics and settings.
Replaced by the in-process ODS engine, which ports model_selection.py and model_memory.py exactly (golden-tested). The FastAPI service can follow on an embedded Python for API parity.
Optional add-on: Open WebUI in an embedded, pinned Python environment (python-build-standalone + uv lock), pointed at the native llama-server.
whisper.cpp server from its official Windows builds (CUDA, Vulkan, CPU), with the same pin, verify and supervise flow as llama.cpp.
A second llama-server in --embedding mode with a pinned GGUF embedding model; TEI has no Windows build.
Kokoro through ONNX Runtime with DirectML (works on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs), behind the same OpenAI-compatible speech API.
The official qdrant.exe Windows release, pinned, with storage under the ODS data folder.
ComfyUI's official Windows portable runtime (embedded Python with CUDA), installed on demand like a model.
n8n on a bundled, pinned Node.js runtime; ODS starter workflows from config/n8n imported on first run.
LiteLLM in the embedded Python environment for cloud and hybrid routing (config/litellm).
SearXNG in the embedded Python environment, served by waitress instead of uWSGI.
Perplexica on the bundled Node.js runtime, wired to SearXNG and the local model.
The official opencode Windows binary, which installers/windows already pins.
Python service in the embedded environment.
Python service in the embedded environment.
Python service in the embedded environment, policy from config/ape.

Portal/Pixel needs a Windows host runtime in place of its systemd units and a sandbox in place of its Docker sandbox. Options: AppContainer + job objects, Windows Sandbox, or an optional WSL backend. Needs a maintainer decision.
Depends on the same agent sandbox decision as Portal; the Windows legacy installer ran it in Docker.
Use the official Tailscale for Windows app; ODS can detect it to offer remote access.
A server-side observability stack (Postgres and ClickHouse); out of scope for a desktop install.
LAN and mDNS entry for headless servers; the desktop app binds to localhost only.
